author: Oluwabukunmi Fakanbi
title: The melodic journey of Stella Monye from 1980s Pop music | The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News
text:
The of Nigerian music has a rich founding legends, but few carry the enduring legacy, cultural weight, and dramatic personal history of Stella Monye. Widely celebrated as the “Samba Queen”, Monye’s remarkable journey spans decades of dynamic artistic evolution, profound personal sacrifice, and a true commitment to the integrity of African sound. As her classic eras continue to influence contemporary discourse, her narrative remains a masterclass in resilience, artistry, and maternal devotion.
The 1980s Pop Pioneer
Long before the modern global Afrobeats boom conquered international charts, Stella Monye was already shaping the blueprint for contemporary African pop. Emerging during an era dominated by legendary record labels like EMI and Tabansi, Monye shot to sudden national prominence with her epochal 1983 debut album Mr. Right, which featured the explosive smash hit “Oko Mi Ye”.
Her infectious fusion of traditional rhythms and pop sensibilities captured the spirit of the 1980s music scene, earning her critical acclaim and massive commercial success. She represented Nigeria on international stages, touring European countries and performing at prestigious cultural gatherings alongside global icons like South African legend Miriam Makeba. Analysts and music historians note that her pioneering use of distinct African grooves predated the widespread international acceptance of contemporary Afro-fusion, establishing her as a true trailblazer of her generation.
Stepping away from the limelight
While her career trajectory pointed toward greater heights, Monye made a conscious, life-altering decision to step back from the limelight. This decision was prompted by a near-tragic accident involving her son, Ibrahim, while she was away on a national musical engagement. Overwhelmed by maternal guilt and a fierce sense of duty, she immediately put her thriving career on hold to navigate a long, grueling medical journey that took them across hospitals in Lagos, India, and eventually New York City.
For years, her life was defined by hospital corridors and continuous surgeries rather than recording studios. Refusing to compromise her role as a mother, Monye carried her cross quietly, transforming her personal pain into a powerful testament of sacrifice. Her journey stands as an enduring symbol of resilience, proving that true heroism often extends far beyond the stage.
Her return to modern digital production
As she gradually re-enters the public eye and adapts to modern digital production techniques releasing inspirational works like her single “He Prepared Me” Monye remains deeply reflective about the trajectory of the Nigerian music industry. Known for her conservative yet vibrant artistic outlook, she has often used her platform to champion socially conscious music.
In recent commentary, the veteran singer has offered candid critiques of contemporary Nigerian tracks, publicly calling on younger artists to look beyond commercial metrics and focus on creating meaningful, message-driven compositions that address societal issues. Despite generational shifts in sound and style, Monye maintains an open and enthusiastic attitude toward modern collaboration, expressing a strong desire to work with today’s generation of chart-topping Afrobeats hitmakers, such as Asake or BNXN. Stella Monye continues to command respect as a timeless pillar of Nigerian musical history.
